current.text: Brooklyn signed him on a mutual option deal as veteran depth.
He is projected as the backup center behind Day'Ron Sharpe. The projected bench rotation includes three big men: Wagner, Noah Clowney and Danny Wolf.
Brooklyn's center minutes are expected to be split, mainly with Sharpe and possibly in a messy three-way split that includes Danny Wolf.
Brooklyn may give more frontcourt minutes to young players like Clowney and Josh Minott in the second half of the season, which makes March minutes for veterans uncertain.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. It does not own its pick, so it has no reason to tank.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3, so 10 games over weeks 19 to 21, with one playoff back-to-back.

durable.text: He is an efficient, high-usage backup big who cannot handle 20-plus minutes a game.

note: Wagner is outside the top 144 on both sites (Yahoo rank 406, ESPN rank 304, 0 USD everywhere). Projections give him only about 9 points and 4 rebounds in roughly 13 minutes, and the experts call him not draftable, so skip him in our auction. Early in the season, check whether Sharpe really starts and how Brooklyn splits center minutes. He only matters as a short-term pickup if Sharpe misses time.
